Two-dimensional ideal-gas Euler flow on [0,4] × [0,1], with gamma = 1.4, a Mach-10 incident shock at 60 degrees, initial shock foot x = 1/6 and final time T = 0.2. The saved reference uses a separately written, unsplit primitive MUSCL/HLL/Heun finite-volume code on 256 × 64 and 512 × 128 cells. Its generalized-minmod slope parameter is theta = 1.5 (MC-type, rather than canonical MC with theta = 2). The primary and reference codes share the HLL flux family and Heun time-integration equations, while their spatial reconstruction and implementations are separate. Conservative restriction produces comparison cell means. Previously executed source, data and receipts are reused from the immutable RKDG2D kit; no reference PDE, Athena or LAVA was executed anew for this addition. Reference grid differences indicate finite-resolution sensitivity, not rigorous error bounds. This is not an analytic 2D solution or a convergence test for the thin wall jet and vortex pattern.
